dentists in this private practice setting did not appear to delay restorative intervention until there were radiographic caries changes in dentin.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dentists in private general practice are not using radiographic evidence of dental caries to determine the timing of restorative treatment.
, on the whole, dentists in this private practice study did not wait until there were radiographic signs of dentin involvement before they placed restorations.
the radiographs of patients in this study did indicate that dentists did not wait for caries to penetrate the dentin before initiating restorative treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of restorations in this study were placed prior to the appearance of radiographically visible caries in the dentin.
